state.task:
Design plugin loading for CLI
The team wants third-party plugins for the ledgerctl CLI. Nobody has agreed on the mechanism. Options mentioned in chat were a dynamic library, a subprocess protocol and a WASM module. The CLI is a single Rust binary in crates/cli. Plugins must be able to add subcommands and read the config file.

Write a design document at docs/design/plugins.md. Compare the three options on security, startup cost, versioning and build complexity. Recommend one. List the decisions that need the product owner before implementation starts. Do not write code for the plugin loader.

Report back: the recommendation in two sentences, the decision list, and the path of the document. Note any assumption you made about the plugin users.

Find lock contention in order service
Under load the order service in orders/services.py shows long waits on the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in reserve_stock(). The stock_items table has an index on sku but not on warehouse_id. Investigate the query plan from logs/explain_reserve.txt, the transaction boundaries in orders/services.py and the retry loop. Identify the root cause of the contention and propose the smallest safe change. Report the query plan lines that support your conclusion.

Design idempotent batch export runner
The export jobs in services/exports run from cron and sometimes run twice for the same day, which duplicates rows in the output bucket. The cron schedule is in ops/cron/exports.txt. Each job writes files named by date and job name.

Read services/exports/internal/job/run.go and the output writer in services/exports/internal/out/. Design an idempotent runner that uses a run record with a unique key of job name plus date. Explain how a second run sees the record and what it does: skip, resume or fail. Explain how a crashed run is detected after a timeout. Write the design to docs/design/export-runner.md.

Report back: the design summary, the state machine in text, the timeout value you chose with its reasoning, and the list of decisions that the owner must confirm.

Plan Redux to Zustand migration
Plan a migration of seven Redux slices in src/store/slices into Zustand stores. The app uses createAsyncThunk in eleven places and reselect selectors in 23 places. Write the migration plan to .agent/plans/zustand-migration.md, with slice order, thunk handling, the compatibility shim needed during the transition, and a rollback. Then migrate only uiSlice to a Zustand store at src/store/ui.ts, keeping the same selector names. Run npx vitest run src/store and report results.

Analyze ambiguous feature for search
The product owner says search should feel smarter. No acceptance criteria are written. The current search lives in search/query.py and uses a simple LIKE on the name column. Clarify what smarter could mean. Describe three concrete variants with their cost in code and infra. Identify what data you need from the team before choosing. Report a short decision memo and do not implement any variant.

Offline sync design for mobile client
Context: the mobile field app in apps/field is a React Native client. Technicians work in basements with no network for up to two days. The app stores work orders locally and must sync them when the network returns. Conflicts happen when a supervisor edits the same work order from the office. The current code has no offline support; the API is in services/workorders.

Your task is a design and a small proof, not the full feature.

1. Read services/workorders/internal/http/workorders.go and list the endpoints the app needs for read, create, update and sync. Note which ones are missing.
2. Read apps/field/src/api/client.ts and check how requests are sent and whether any retry exists.
3. Design the local store: a table for work orders, a table for a write queue with fields id, entity, op, payload, created_at and attempts, and a rule for the order of queue replay. Use SQLite through the library already listed in apps/field/package.json. Do not add a library.
4. Define the conflict rule. Options are last write wins, server wins, and field-level merge. Pick one for the fields status, notes and assignee and justify it with the business rule in docs/requirements/workorders.md.
5. Write a proof: apps/field/src/sync/queue.ts with a function enqueue and a function replay that takes a fake transport. Add apps/field/src/sync/queue.test.ts with three tests: replay in order, a failed item stays queued with attempts incremented, and a success removes the item. Run npx vitest run src/sync in apps/field.
6. Write the design in docs/design/offline-sync.md under 1,000 words.

Constraints: do not change the server API. Do not add a dependency. Do not store auth tokens in the queue table.

Report back: the missing endpoints, the local schema, the conflict rule with its reason, the vitest result line, and the list of open questions for the product owner.

Add Go CLI subcommand for backup
In the Go project at tools/backupctl add a subcommand verify to cmd/root.go using cobra. verify takes a --path flag pointing to a tar.gz archive and checks that the archive opens and contains a manifest.json file at its root. Return exit code 0 when valid and 2 when invalid, printing the reason to stderr. Put the logic in internal/verify/verify.go with a function Check(path string) error. Add a table test in internal/verify/verify_test.go. Run go test ./internal/verify/... and report the result.

Form wizard step validation
Add per-step validation to the onboarding wizard in src/features/onboarding/Wizard.tsx. The wizard has three steps defined in src/features/onboarding/steps.ts: company, team, and billing. Each step has a zod schema. The Next button must validate only the fields of the current step and move forward only when they are valid. The Back button never validates.
Implementation: create src/features/onboarding/useWizardValidation.ts exporting useWizardValidation(steps, currentIndex, values) that returns { canAdvance, errors }. Use schema.safeParse on the current step only. Map zod issues to a record keyed by field path. Do not run the validation on mount; only run it after the user presses Next once, tracked in a useState flag named attempted.
Accessibility: when validation fails, move focus to the first invalid input using a ref map keyed by field name, and announce the error count in a visually hidden role status element. Do not change the existing markup of the inputs.
Tests: add src/features/onboarding/Wizard.test.tsx covering Next blocked on invalid company name, Next allowed when valid, Back allowed with invalid data, focus moved to the first invalid field, and the status text shows the count, for example '2 errors'.
Run npx vitest run src/features/onboarding and report the summary line. Run npx tsc --noEmit and report the exit code.
Report back with the files changed, the summary line, the typecheck exit code, and the exact status text produced in the test where two fields are invalid.

Add reusable CI workflow for Go services
Context: each Go service repeats the same five CI jobs in its own workflow file. Copy-paste has drifted: three services cache modules and two do not. Create one reusable workflow and call it from one service workflow as a pilot. Leave the other services alone.

Requirements:
1. Create .github/workflows/go-service-ci.yml with on: workflow_call. Inputs: service_dir (string, required), go_version (string, default 1.23), and run_integration (boolean, default false).
2. The reusable workflow has three jobs: lint, unit and integration. Job lint runs golangci-lint with the config at .golangci.yml from the repo root. Job unit runs go test -race -count=1 in the service directory. Job integration runs only when run_integration is true and runs go test -tags=integration in the service directory.
3. All three jobs use actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-go@v5 with go-version set from the input and cache enabled. Set cache-dependency-path to the service directory plus /go.sum.
4. Add a job output named coverage that the unit job exposes. Compute the total coverage from go tool cover -func and write it to the job output. Use the step output mechanism of GitHub Actions and write to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
5. Replace the body of .github/workflows/billing-api.yml with a single job that calls the reusable workflow with service_dir set to services/billing-api and run_integration set to true. Keep the existing on: triggers of billing-api.yml exactly as they are.
6. Use permissions: contents: read at the top of the reusable workflow. Do not add any secret.

Constraints:
- Do not change any other service workflow file.
- Do not add a matrix over services in this change.
- Keep the job names lint, unit and integration exactly.
- Do not use the deprecated set-output command.

Checks:
- actionlint .github/workflows/go-service-ci.yml .github/workflows/billing-api.yml must print no errors.
- grep -n "set-output" .github/workflows/go-service-ci.yml must print no lines.
- grep -n "GITHUB_OUTPUT" .github/workflows/go-service-ci.yml must print the coverage line.

Report back: the two files changed, the actionlint output, the grep outputs, and the coverage line you wrote. If actionlint is not installed, install nothing; report that and stop.

Change owner header in migration files
Context: the data platform group was renamed to platform-data. Migration files 0030 to 0039 under db/migrations/ have a header comment line that names the old owner. Change that owner line in those ten files only. Do not change the migration SQL.

The header line in each file currently reads:
-- owner: data-team

Change it to:
-- owner: platform-data

Steps:
1. Run ls db/migrations to list the file names. Identify the files whose name starts with 0030_ through 0039_. There should be ten files. If the count differs, stop and report the names you found.
2. In each of those files, change the owner line to the new text. If a file has no owner line, do not add one; list that file in your report.
3. Run grep -rn "owner: data-team" db/migrations and report any hit that is not in files 0030 to 0039.
4. Run git diff --stat -- db/migrations and confirm that only the ten files changed, each with a one-line change.
5. Run sqlfluff lint db/migrations/0030_*.sql db/migrations/0031_*.sql if sqlfluff is installed. Report the result. If it is not installed, say so.

Constraints: do not rename any migration file. Do not change checksums stored in the migrate table. Do not run any migration against a database.

Report back: the list of ten files, each with changed or skipped status, the grep hits outside the range, and the git diff stat line. Confirm that no SQL statement changed.

Fix staging label in Kubernetes manifests
In deploy/k8s/*.yaml change the metadata.labels value env from staging to stage. Do not change env var values. Run kubeconform -strict deploy/k8s/ and report the summary line.

Add YAML output to ledgerctl report
Context: the report command in crates/cli prints a table or JSON. Finance wants YAML output for a tool that reads the files. Add a --format yaml option. Keep the default and the JSON output unchanged.

Current code:
- crates/cli/src/commands/report.rs defines the command and an enum OutputFormat with variants Table and Json.
- crates/cli/src/output/mod.rs has the functions render_table and render_json that take a slice of ReportRow.
- ReportRow is in crates/cli/src/model.rs and derives serde::Serialize.
- crates/cli/Cargo.toml does not list serde_yaml.

Requirements:
1. Add the variant Yaml to OutputFormat. The clap value name is yaml.
2. Add render_yaml in crates/cli/src/output/yaml.rs that returns a String. It uses serde_yaml::to_string on the slice of rows.
3. Add the crate serde_yaml to crates/cli/Cargo.toml with a version that is already in the workspace Cargo.lock. Check Cargo.lock first with grep -n 'name = "serde_yaml"' Cargo.lock. If the crate is not in the lock file, stop and report that. Do not add a new version by hand-editing Cargo.lock.
4. The output uses the same field order as JSON. Do not add a header comment.
5. An empty report must print the YAML empty list [] and exit 0.
6. The table and JSON paths must not change. Run the existing tests before and after your change and report both counts.

Constraints:
- Do not add a new subcommand.
- Do not change the ReportRow struct fields or their serde attributes.
- Keep rename_all = "snake_case" behavior the same as JSON.

Tests:
- crates/cli/tests/report_yaml.rs runs the binary against tests/data/report_small.csv with --format yaml and parses stdout with serde_yaml::from_str into a Vec of maps. It checks the row count and the first id.
- A unit test for render_yaml with an empty slice.

Commands:
- cargo test -p ledger-cli (run once before your change and once after)
- cargo clippy -p ledger-cli -- -D warnings

Report back: files changed, the test counts before and after, clippy result, the serde_yaml version found in Cargo.lock, and the first 4 lines of the YAML output for the small fixture.

Write date range validator
Write isValidRange(start: Date, end: Date): boolean in src/lib/dates.ts. True when start is not after end and the span is at most 366 days. Add Jest tests for equal dates, reversed dates, and a 367-day span. Run npx jest src/lib/dates.

Add coverage target to Makefile
Add a Makefile target named coverage. It runs go test -coverprofile=coverage.out ./... and then go tool cover -func=coverage.out and writes the total line to the console. The target must fail with a non-zero exit code when the total coverage is below the value in the variable COVER_MIN, which defaults to 70. Add the target to the .PHONY line. Add a line to the help target that describes it. Run make coverage and report the exit code and the total line. Use a shell test for the threshold check, not an awk one-liner that is hard to read.

Add JSON schema check to config loader
The config loader in config/loader.py reads YAML and passes it straight into the app. Add a validation step that checks the loaded dict against the JSON schema in config/schema/app.schema.json using the jsonschema package already listed in requirements/base.txt. On failure raise ConfigError with the first three validation messages joined by semicolons. Add a test in config/tests/test_loader.py with one valid and one invalid sample file under config/tests/data/. Run pytest config -q and paste the summary.

Update HTML email footer text
Context: the transactional email templates in mailer/templates/ all end with a footer that still names the old support address line text 'Questions? Write to the support desk.' The marketing team wants the footer to read 'Questions? Contact our help center.' in every template. The footer block is the last div with class footer in each file. The templates are Django templates, so do not change any template tag or variable.

Steps: list the template files with ls mailer/templates/*.html. For each file, confirm the footer sentence appears exactly once with grep -n. Replace only that sentence with the new text, keeping the surrounding HTML and whitespace exactly the same. Some files are in mailer/templates/legacy/ and must not change, because they are kept for old clients. Skip them and list them in the report.

Constraints: do not modify the CSS in mailer/templates/base.html. Do not change links or the copyright year in the footer. Do not change the plain text versions in mailer/templates/text/ unless they contain the same sentence, in which case update that sentence too and mention it in the report.

Verification: run grep -rn "support desk" mailer/templates/ and paste the output, which should only show the legacy files. Run python manage.py test mailer -q if the mailer test suite exists, and report the pass count. If the test suite does not exist, say so.

Report back: the number of templates you changed, the list of skipped legacy files, the list of text versions you changed, and the grep output. Keep the report short, under 20 lines, with file paths written in full.

Add user-agent header to HTTP client
In the Python package partner_sync the class PartnerApiClient in partner_sync/client.py builds its requests session without a user agent. Add the header User-Agent with the value partner-sync/<version>, where version comes from the attribute __version__ in partner_sync/__init__.py.

Set the header once when the session is created in the constructor. Do not add the header to each request call. Keep the public method signatures unchanged.

Add a test in tests/test_client.py that creates the client with a mocked session and checks the header value starts with partner-sync/.

Run pytest tests/test_client.py -q and report the summary. Then run python3 -m ruff check partner_sync and report the count of issues.

Context: the partner team filters traffic by the prefix of the User-Agent header, and the prefix must stay exactly partner-sync/ followed by the version. Do not add any other text to the header value.
Context: the same client class is copied into the batch project under batch/partner/client.py without the header. Leave the copy unchanged and note in the report that the batch copy has no User-Agent header.
Report back: the summary line, the ruff count, and the file names you changed.

Fix CI badge URL in README
Update the CI badge URL in README.md from org name acme-old to acme-labs. Only that line changes. Report the line number.

Pin Docker node base images
The Dockerfiles in services/api, services/worker, and services/cron use node:18-alpine. Change each FROM line to node:20.11-alpine3.19. Do not change any other instruction. If docker is available, run docker build for each file. If it is not, run hadolint on all three files and report its output. Report which files you edited.

Update Ktor version in libs
The file gradle/libs.versions.toml in the mobile-backend repo pins ktor at 2.3.7. Change the value to 2.3.12 and nothing else. Run ./gradlew :backend:dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath | grep ktor-server-core and paste the first matching line.
